DisplayName: Multi-team software delivery and release governance
Summary: .NET-focused multi-team delivery template for planned software change with explicit app-type classification, architecture design and review, subprocess-backed implementation, QA, runtime command writeback, UI screenshot writeback, security, release, deployment, and retrospective governance.
ValueStatement: Delivers .NET application changes through typed, observable subprocesses that keep architecture, implementation, validation, runtime commands, screenshots, release authority, and project-structure evidence explicit.
InterfaceContractSummary: The process targets .NET software delivery first: backend-only/API/service, Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, worker, console, library, or mixed solution. JavaScript-specific delivery should use a separate process rather than hidden branching here.
GovernanceNotes: Architecture, implementation, validation, runtime command writeback, screenshot writeback, security, and release gates have explicit operation contracts. `allowedOperations` and `operationTargetScope` must stay source-aligned with the canonical ProcessStepOperation and ProcessStepTargetScope catalogs. Architects and QA reviewers do not mutate product files; implementation and repair remain the only product-mutable lanes.
ChangeSummary: Hardens multi-team software delivery for .NET by routing architecture design/review, implementation, runtime command writeback, and UI screenshot writeback through subprocesses with explicit permissions.
GovernancePolicySummary: Release readiness requires reviewed .NET architecture, implementation evidence, QA evidence, security posture, Run command nodes, UI screenshot or no-UI evidence, rollback readiness, and explicit residual-risk ownership.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Role contracts, decision rights, and source-of-truth ownership outlive the specific person or agent assigned at runtime.
OperatingModeSummary: Governed live execution is allowed only after explicit quality acceptance, security review, and release gates succeed.
SimulationReadinessSummary: This template is intentionally rich enough for simulation, canvas authoring, analytics, and large-screen browser walkthroughs.
Metrics: Median time from approved scope boundary to architecture decision record.
Share of releases approved without rollback-plan defects.
Percentage of release approvals with complete QA, security, and rollback artifact inputs.
Rate of releases requiring rollback or controlled halt inside the first telemetry window.
Number of corrective actions closed from post-release learning within the committed SLA.
Risks: Architecture drift if implementation bypasses the approved canonical-model decision.
Weak release decisions if artifact inputs are missing or stale.
False confidence when QA evidence is verbal instead of durable.
Security exceptions hidden inside release pressure.
Rollout instability when telemetry watch points or rollback triggers are implicit.
TailoringRules: Low-risk internal changes may shorten QA depth, but the release-approval step still requires explicit artifact inputs.
If no sensitive-data, secrets, or trust boundary is touched, security review may downgrade to reviewer status rather than full approver blocking power.
Multiple implementation slices may be modeled as separate work steps, but all must converge into the same release-approval artifact-input contract.
Validation or review findings must route through an explicit repair branch when a modeled repair branch exists; use blocked status only when the role cannot produce a governed disposition.
Hotfix or incident-driven work must use the dedicated emergency template rather than bypassing this one.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Convert business intent into an explicit delivery contract with clear acceptance boundaries and prioritized value trade-offs.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: One accountable human decision-maker who can clarify scope, decide priority, accept delivered outcomes, and absorb stakeholder escalation without routing every decision through engineering.
RoleUsages.Notes: Outcome and acceptance owner for value, scope, sequencing, and release acceptance.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Keep the process executable by turning desired outcomes into a feasible, staffed, time-aware delivery path with explicit escalation triggers.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior delivery-side coordinator with enough authority to challenge unrealistic dates, surface hidden dependencies, and keep multiple roles synchronized.
RoleUsages.Notes: Flow owner for sequencing, staffing realism, dependency control, and execution escalation.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Protect maintainability and operability by reviewing design options, target architecture fit, and downstream integration impact before costly implementation commitment.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior technical authority who can reason across components, environments, data boundaries, and operational consequences.
RoleUsages.Notes: Architecture authority for system boundaries, irreversible decisions, and cross-domain technical coherence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own the change set and keep implementation evidence aligned with the approved architecture and release boundary.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Build-capable engineering owner for the working change set and adjacent test evidence.
RoleUsages.Notes: Implementation owner for code, tests, migration notes, and executable delivery proof.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Challenge whether the delivered change is proven enough for its risk profile and make test evidence decision-ready for release governance.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior test leader able to shape strategy, select evidence depth, and identify where automation is not enough.
RoleUsages.Notes: Quality owner for coverage depth, evidence quality, and release confidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Coordinate go-live preparation and keep rollback and telemetry watch ownership explicit before and during release execution.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Operational owner for production execution, release windows, and rollback decisions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Operational owner for rollout control, rollback readiness, and telemetry review.

Steps.Title: Clarify .NET scope and app type boundary
Steps.Subtitle: .NET delivery contract and no-go constraints
Steps.Notes: Capture the requested outcome, user or operational impact, target delivery window, known dependencies, explicit exclusions, and .NET delivery target. Classify or request classification evidence for backend-only/API/service, Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, worker, console, library, or mixed solution. Preserve explicit project-structure requirements as source-of-truth constraints; they must not be downgraded to optional, excluded, or follow-up work unless the project structure or an accepted decision record says so.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Requested change, impact notes, target delivery window, and stakeholder-facing constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Decision-ready .NET scope packet with acceptance boundary, app-type hypothesis, dependency map, assumptions, exclusions, and validation hooks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Intake notes, acceptance criteria, .NET app-type hypothesis, product root hints, UI/no-UI hints, run/test command hints, known exclusions, assumptions, and unresolved dependency register.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Product owner can refine the ask but cannot waive architecture, data, or release-governance requirements.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Escalate immediately when timeline pressure conflicts with data-safety or release constraints.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: If the original product owner changes, ownership transfers to the next accountable value owner without changing the process contract.
Delivery review remains explicit even if staffing changes mid-stream.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Scope boundary packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable during architecture review, implementation planning, and future scope-drift analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture no-go constraints, user or operational impact, acceptance boundary, .NET app-type hypothesis, product root hints, UI/no-UI hints, and run/test command hints. Must preserve explicit project-structure source-of-truth requirements without downgrading them to optional, excluded, non-acceptance, or follow-up work unless the project structure itself says the item is optional or deferred.

Steps.Title: Run .NET architecture design and review subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Design, challenge, and app-type routing
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the .NET architecture design and review subprocess. The child process must classify the app type, draft architecture, independently review the design, and return implementation-ready architecture evidence with any mandatory implementation constraints. This parent step coordinates the subprocess and must not perform product mutation or implementation work.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Scope packet, project-structure context, requested .NET deliverable, and acceptance criteria.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child architecture run with app-type classification, reviewed design decision, implementation-ready handoff, mandatory implementation constraints, and unresolved architecture risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, .NET app classification, architecture decision, review findings, implementation constraints, implementation start criteria, and UI/no-UI applicability.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect owns the visible architecture subprocess assignment and reviewed handoff; delivery manager remains an explicit coordination reviewer.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the child architecture subprocess blocks, fails, or returns missing app type, design review, or implementation-ready handoff evidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture subprocess ownership stays with a role-compatible technical authority that can review design evidence without implementing code.
Delivery manager reviews subprocess sequencing and escalation without taking architecture authority.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Project structure context brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for implementation, review, QA, security, runtime command writeback, screenshot writeback, and release decisions.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must map to child app classification evidence and capture process run node, product root, test root, .NET app type, UI/no-UI applicability, runtime surfaces, and downstream artifact expectations.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Architecture decision record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for implementation, review, QA, runtime command writeback, screenshot writeback, and later forensic replay.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must map to the reviewed child architecture handoff and include selected option, rejected options, source-of-truth choice, service/model/component boundaries, testability notes, and migration ownership.

Steps.Title: Run .NET implementation slice subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Observed implementation and validation slice
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the .NET implementation slice subprocess for the approved scope and architecture. When the approved scope is a full app or broad deliverable, launch the child with a first reviewable MVP implementation slice derived from feature-intake and architecture artifacts. The MVP slice must not be scaffold-only, app-shell-only, setup-only, naming-only, or build-only proof; it must include the smallest observable product-specific path a user can exercise. When project structure lists visual target assets, carry their ImageAsset node ids and media paths into the child implementation request as source design inputs. The child implementation must use those assets to shape the visible UI, not only the text summary. The child implementation slice owns solution setup, feature/function implementation, repair subprocesses, tests, targeted proof, and accepted handoff evidence. This parent step records child-run evidence and does not mutate product files directly. This parent step must not launch the app, navigate a browser, wait on browser state, capture screenshots, or perform viewport/runtime proof directly; those actions belong to child targeted validation and later runtime/screenshot writeback steps that include LaunchRuntime and CaptureRuntimeProof.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved .NET architecture path, app classification, scope packet, unresolved technical questions, and implementation-slice start criteria.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child implementation slice with reviewable change set, test evidence, blockers, rollout inputs, accepted parent-ready handoff, or explicit repair escalation evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, change-set projection, validation outputs, accepted handoff evidence, repair escalation evidence, output-placement notes, migration steps when applicable, touched-surface inventory, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Lead engineer owns the visible implementation subprocess assignment and accepted handoff; delivery manager remains an explicit coordination reviewer.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the child implementation slice blocks, fails, omits required project-structure requirements, lacks accepted handoff evidence, or returns slice-repair-escalation. Do not treat a completed child run with an escalation/no-go packet as accepted implementation proof. If accepted child evidence is missing, record a blocker or repair escalation instead of attempting browser proof from this parent step.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Implementation subprocess ownership stays with a role-compatible engineering agent that can own technical handoff evidence.
Delivery manager reviews child implementation sequencing and escalation without editing product code.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for peer review, QA, runtime command writeback, screenshot writeback, release approval, and later defect forensics.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to the observed .NET implementation slice child run and include changed files, behavioral intent, validation proof tied to acceptance criteria, accepted handoff evidence from slice-handoff or slice-handoff-after-repair, and confirmation that explicit project-structure requirements were not dropped or deferred. A slice-repair-escalation packet is blocker evidence, not accepted implementation proof.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Migration and rollout preparation checklist
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release rehearsal and rollback planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name data changes or none, operational preconditions, publish/output-placement steps, rollback/removal steps, and accepted child-run handoff evidence used to derive them. Accept either slice-handoff or slice-handoff-after-repair as the source; do not use slice-repair-escalation as rollout-ready evidence.

Steps.Title: Complete peer review and integration readiness
Steps.Subtitle: Design and implementation challenge
Steps.Notes: Review the change set against the approved design, integration consequences, and release assumptions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Implementation package, architecture decision record, and changed-surface inventory.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Peer-reviewed change set with explicit residual risk and follow-up items.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Review notes, unresolved issues list, and approved follow-up actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Reviewers may block unsafe merge or release progression until the change set satisfies design and evidence expectations.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not downgrade architecture, data, or migration concerns to cosmetic comments.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Implementation owner remains attached until review comments are addressed.
Architectural review remains explicit when cross-module consequences exist.
QA participates when changed surface suggests regression risk.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Peer review note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for QA, security, and release governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture accepted issues, rejected concerns, and explicit residual risk.

Steps.Title: Run QA validation and runtime or browser proof
Steps.Subtitle: Regression, UX, runtime, and quality evidence
Steps.Notes: Execute targeted regression, runtime/API/browser proof as applicable, and defect triage against the reviewed implementation package. When project structure, scope, or implementation evidence identifies a visible browser workflow, capture current-run process-visible browser artifacts under `artifacts/process-runs/<run-id>/browser/` before selecting quality-accepted. When project structure lists visual target assets, QA must use those ImageAsset node ids and media paths as source visual requirements. Fetch or analyze the relevant asset content, then compare the delivered screenshot against the target image before accepting visual alignment. Do not accept visual quality from the delivered screenshot alone. The final QA artifact must include a `Visual target comparison` section naming the source ImageAsset node id, media path or file name, source asset fetch or analysis receipt, delivered screenshot ref, comparison method, and acceptance or repair-required disposition. For every screenshot used to accept or reject a visual claim, call `workspace_analyze_image` and cite the current execution run, provider, model, token counts, and tool receipt path or id. For before/after comparisons, animated behavior, queued work, background loading, polling, timers, streaming, or any claim that visible state changes over time, capture ordered screenshots over elapsed time and call `workspace_analyze_images`. If image analysis is unavailable but current browser snapshot/evaluate output, console evidence, screenshot inspection, and validation receipts are enough to identify a repairable defect or proof gap, return status Completed with branchOutcomeKey repair-required. Return Blocked only for a confirmed tool, policy, environment, access, or process-contract failure that prevents QA from collecting enough evidence to choose quality-accepted or repair-required; cite the failed tool, provider/model, and receipt or missing capability.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Peer-reviewed change set, changed-surface inventory, and release-scope assumptions.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Targeted QA result with runtime/API/browser evidence as applicable, regressions, warning and executed-test counts, shipped entrypoint/runtime consistency, residual quality risk, and an explicit accepted or repair-required branch. Browser-workflow quality acceptance requires process-visible screenshot, current-run `workspace_analyze_image` or `workspace_analyze_images` receipt for visual claims, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output, actual URL or entrypoint, launch and cleanup receipts, acceptance-state assertion, and a `Visual target comparison` section when source ImageAsset targets exist.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Regression logs, warning-free validation output unless explicitly accepted, nonzero executed-test proof when tests are expected, shipped entrypoint plus referenced-runtime inspection, stale or unreferenced artifact assessment, runtime/API/browser proof as applicable, screenshots for UI surfaces, source ImageAsset node id/media path evidence when visual targets exist, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual conclusions, defect notes, and current-run process-visible browser artifacts when a visible browser workflow is in scope.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA lead selects an explicit quality disposition: accepted evidence may continue, while reproducible defects or proof gaps route to repair.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not let schedule pressure replace proof with verbal confidence. Artifact recovery: route missing or invalid QA evidence, browser/runtime proof, or repair-required evidence to repair-required when the implementation role can repair it. Block only when a confirmed tool, policy, environment, access, or process-contract failure prevents branch routing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: QA ownership may move across qualified reviewers without collapsing the gate.
Implementation owner reviews failures and fixes before release approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Regression evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release approval, incident review, and later regression comparison.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name changed flows, assertion depth, warning counts, executed-test counts when tests are expected, shipped entrypoint and referenced runtime files or commands, runtime/API/browser evidence as applicable, screenshots for UI surfaces, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual conclusions, stale/unreferenced artifact findings, and unresolved risks. When the current project structure, scope packet, or implementation evidence identifies a visible browser workflow, the pack must include current-run process-visible browser artifacts under `artifacts/process-runs/<run-id>/browser/`: screenshot image, current-run `workspace_analyze_image` receipt for visual screenshot decisions, current-run `workspace_analyze_images` receipt for ordered comparisons or time-dependent behavior, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output showing no active JavaScript/runtime errors, actual URL or entrypoint, launch and cleanup receipts, and an acceptance-state assertion mapped to the project-structure notes. When source ImageAsset targets exist, the pack must also include a `Visual target comparison` section naming the source ImageAsset node id, media path or file name, source asset fetch or analysis receipt, delivered screenshot ref, comparison method, and quality-accepted or repair-required disposition. Missing, empty, detached, stale, or chat-only browser proof must route to repair-required.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Quality accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: QA evidence is sufficient for downstream security and release governance.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Repair required
BranchOutcomes.Description: QA found reproducible defects, missing workflows, failed validation, or proof gaps that the implementation role must repair before release governance.

Steps.Title: Repair validation findings
Steps.Subtitle: Focused rework from QA evidence
Steps.Notes: Repair concrete defects, missing workflows, failed validation, or proof gaps identified by QA without expanding beyond the approved delivery scope.
Steps.InputContractSummary: QA repair-required disposition, reviewed implementation package, and failing proof details.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Repaired change set and validation notes ready for QA recheck.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Changed files or deliverables, repair rationale, rerun validation, and remaining risks.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Lead engineer owns repair execution inside the approved scope and must escalate scope expansion instead of hiding it.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not mark repair complete until the defect cause is addressed and required validation has been rerun.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Repair ownership remains with the implementation role so QA findings result in concrete fixes.
QA remains available to clarify failing evidence without taking ownership of implementation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Quality repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for QA recheck, security review, release approval, and later defect analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name repaired defects, changed files or deliverables, rerun validation, and unresolved risk.

Steps.Title: Re-run QA validation and runtime or browser proof after repair
Steps.Subtitle: Repair verification
Steps.Notes: Re-run targeted runtime/API/browser validation as applicable against the repaired package and select an explicit accepted or unresolved-repair branch. When project structure, original QA findings, or repair evidence identifies a visible browser workflow, recapture current-run process-visible browser artifacts under `artifacts/process-runs/<run-id>/browser/` before selecting quality-accepted. When project structure lists visual target assets, QA recheck must use those ImageAsset node ids and media paths as source visual requirements. Fetch or analyze the relevant asset content again if the prior receipt is missing, then compare the repaired screenshot against the target image before accepting visual alignment. Do not accept visual quality from the repaired screenshot alone. For every screenshot used to accept or reject a repaired visual claim, call `workspace_analyze_image` and cite the current execution run, provider, model, token counts, and tool receipt path or id. For before/after comparisons, animated behavior, queued work, background loading, polling, timers, streaming, or any claim that visible state changes over time, capture ordered screenshots over elapsed time and call `workspace_analyze_images`. If image analysis is unavailable but current browser snapshot/evaluate output, console evidence, screenshot inspection, and validation receipts are enough to identify an unresolved repair defect or proof gap, return status Completed with branchOutcomeKey repair-escalation. Return Blocked only for a confirmed tool, policy, environment, access, or process-contract failure that prevents QA from collecting enough evidence to choose quality-accepted or repair-escalation; cite the failed tool, provider/model, and receipt or missing capability.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Repair change set, original QA findings, and reviewed implementation package.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Recheck result with warning-free validation, nonzero executed-test proof when tests are expected, shipped entrypoint/runtime consistency, runtime/API/browser evidence as applicable, regression evidence, and explicit quality disposition. Browser-workflow repair acceptance requires fresh process-visible screenshot, current-run `workspace_analyze_image` or `workspace_analyze_images` receipt for visual claims, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output, actual URL or entrypoint, launch and cleanup receipts, acceptance-state assertion, and a `Visual target comparison` section when source ImageAsset targets exist.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Regression logs, warning-free validation output unless explicitly accepted, nonzero executed-test proof when tests are expected, shipped entrypoint plus referenced-runtime inspection, stale or unreferenced artifact assessment, runtime/API/browser proof as applicable, screenshots for UI surfaces, source ImageAsset node id/media path evidence when visual targets exist, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for repaired visual conclusions, repair verification, unresolved defects if any, and fresh current-run process-visible browser artifacts when a visible browser workflow is in scope.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA lead may accept the repaired evidence or escalate when repair remains insufficient.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: select repair-escalation when the required repaired regression evidence artifact is missing, invalid, or proves the same failing flow, launch, or proof gap remains unresolved. Block only when a confirmed tool, policy, environment, access, or process-contract failure prevents repaired QA recheck from choosing quality-accepted or repair-escalation.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: QA owns the repaired quality disposition.
Implementation owner reviews remaining findings before release governance continues.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Repaired regression evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for post-repair security review, release approval, and later regression comparison.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name repaired flows, assertion depth, warning counts, executed-test counts when tests are expected, shipped entrypoint and referenced runtime files or commands, runtime/API/browser evidence as applicable, screenshots for UI surfaces, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for repaired visual conclusions, stale/unreferenced artifact findings, and unresolved risks after the repair pass. When the current project structure, original QA findings, or repair evidence identifies a visible browser workflow, the pack must include fresh current-run process-visible browser artifacts under `artifacts/process-runs/<run-id>/browser/`: screenshot image, current-run `workspace_analyze_image` receipt for visual screenshot decisions, current-run `workspace_analyze_images` receipt for ordered comparisons or time-dependent behavior, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output showing no active JavaScript/runtime errors, actual URL or entrypoint, launch and cleanup receipts, and an acceptance-state assertion mapped to the project-structure notes. When source ImageAsset targets exist, the pack must also include a `Visual target comparison` section naming the source ImageAsset node id, media path or file name, source asset fetch or analysis receipt, repaired screenshot ref, comparison method, and quality-accepted or repair-escalation disposition. Missing, empty, detached, stale, or chat-only browser proof must route to repair-escalation.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Quality accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: Repaired evidence is sufficient for downstream security and release governance.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Repair escalation
BranchOutcomes.Description: The same or new release-blocking quality issue remains after repair and needs explicit delivery escalation.

Steps.Title: Perform security and data-handling review
Steps.Subtitle: Sensitive data, secrets, and exception posture
Steps.Notes: Review sensitive-data handling, secrets, boundary changes, and policy exceptions only after first-pass QA accepts the quality evidence. Scale findings to the declared release boundary instead of inventing production controls that are outside the approved handoff.
Steps.InputContractSummary: QA-accepted package, changed-surface inventory, and data-handling notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Security outcome with explicit approval, block, or exception rationale tied to the declared release boundary.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security review notes, exception rationale, boundary-applicable controls, and future production controls when they are outside the current boundary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer owns the sign-off for sensitive-data and boundary-applicable policy exceptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block release when current-boundary data-handling review capacity is missing, exception rationale is incomplete, or a security risk affects the approved handoff. Record out-of-boundary production controls as recommendations unless explicitly required.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security approval remains attached to the role even if the reviewer changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Security exception assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release governance, audit, and post-incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture boundary-applicable controls, residual risk owner, approval or block rationale, and any future controls that are not release blockers for the current boundary.

Steps.Title: Record .NET run commands under process run node
Steps.Subtitle: Run command, Run app, Run tests
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the .NET runtime command writeback subprocess after first-pass QA acceptance. It must create or update runtime-capable Run app and Run tests nodes under the current process run node, using Environment nodes for runnable .NET app launch commands and Script nodes for test/build/utility commands. It must not write runnable commands as delivery blocks. The child handoff must include launcher-compatible metadata receipts for every runnable command node; do not accept a Run app or Run tests node as complete when it lacks the project path, command, arguments, working directory, subtype, or other metadata needed by the project-structure runtime launcher. This step coordinates subprocess evidence only and does not mutate product files.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Accepted QA evidence, architecture handoff, implementation evidence, and process run node context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed .NET runtime command project-structure writeback child run with parent-ready evidence for runtime-capable Run app and Run tests nodes.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, managed artifacts, project-structure receipts, node ids, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Parent role coordinates subprocess completion and cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Inspect stopped child subprocess evidence before blocking. If required child evidence is missing and relaunch is allowed, relaunch through the subprocess driver; block only for concrete missing tools, inputs, policy/environment failures, or irrecoverable evidence after a fresh child result.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a role-compatible operator that can observe the subprocess and record parent evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET Run command writeback
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by release approval and process-run replay.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to child step runtime-command-handoff, include child artifact .NET runtime command handoff, current process run node context, write receipts, and unresolved blockers.

Steps.Title: Capture and store .NET UI screenshots
Steps.Subtitle: Screenshots under process run node
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the .NET UI screenshot writeback subprocess after runtime command nodes exist. UI targets must capture screenshots and store accepted image assets under a Screenshots parent node below the current process run node. Backend-only or no-UI targets must produce explicit no-UI evidence. When a child screenshot handoff accepts or rejects screenshots for visual reasons, verify that the child evidence includes current-run `workspace_analyze_image` receipts for individual screenshots and `workspace_analyze_images` receipts for ordered comparisons or time-dependent behavior. Do not complete from screenshot paths, dimensions, or project-structure image asset ids alone when the downstream decision depends on visual content. Write the parent step record to artifacts/process-runs/<current-process-run-id>/steps/capture-ui-screenshots.md and include that exact path in final evidenceRefs together with child screenshot handoff evidence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Accepted QA evidence, architecture handoff, implementation evidence, and process run node context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed .NET UI screenshot project-structure writeback child run with parent-ready writeback evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, managed artifacts, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual screenshot decisions, project-structure receipts, node ids, screenshot or no-UI receipts, runtime command compatibility evidence, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Parent role coordinates subprocess completion and cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Inspect stopped child subprocess evidence before blocking. If required child evidence is missing and relaunch is allowed, relaunch through the subprocess driver; block only for concrete missing tools, inputs, policy/environment failures, or irrecoverable evidence after a fresh child result.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a role-compatible operator that can observe the subprocess and record parent evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot writeback
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by release approval and process-run replay.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include the current-run parent step artifact path artifacts/process-runs/<current-process-run-id>/steps/capture-ui-screenshots.md in final evidenceRefs, point to child step screenshot-handoff, include child artifact .NET UI screenshot writeback handoff, current process run node context, Screenshots parent node, accepted image asset or no-UI receipts, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual screenshot decisions, write receipts, and unresolved blockers.

Steps.Title: Approve first-pass release readiness
Steps.Subtitle: Go / no-go board decision
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject release using first-pass QA proof, shipped entrypoint/runtime consistency, security posture, rollback readiness, support coverage, and the declared release boundary. Conditions must apply to the approved boundary; out-of-boundary production hardening belongs in future recommendations unless explicitly required. When release approval depends on visual UI claims, require current-run `workspace_analyze_image` or `workspace_analyze_images` receipts from QA or screenshot writeback evidence. Do not approve from screenshot file paths, dimensions, project-structure image asset ids, or chat summaries alone.
Steps.InputContractSummary: QA evidence that names the shipped entrypoint and referenced runtime, security outcome, Run command nodes, UI screenshot or no-UI evidence with provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual UI claims, rollback/removal plan, support ownership, and declared release boundary.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected release readiness with accountable rationale and boundary-applicable conditions only.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval note, residual risk register, rollback/removal ownership record, declared-boundary confirmation, Run command node references, Screenshots parent/image asset or no-UI evidence, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for visual approval claims, and confirmation that QA proof matches the actual shipped entrypoint rather than stale or unreferenced artifacts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns the decision and cannot waive missing proof or missing rollback readiness silently.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject release when security review, Run command nodes, UI screenshot/no-UI evidence, rollback/removal ownership, support readiness, or proof required by the declared release boundary remains incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Release approval belongs to the accountable delivery manager role, not to whichever person attended a meeting.
Operational release owner reviews rollback and support readiness before the board decision.

Steps.Title: Execute first-pass controlled release rollout
Steps.Subtitle: Boundary-scoped release execution and watch
Steps.Notes: Deploy, publish, export, or hand off the approved deliverable inside the declared release boundary while rollback, removal, or recovery readiness remains explicit. Use live telemetry only when the boundary includes a live service or production host.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved release record, delivery package or artifact root, rollback or removal plan, declared release boundary, and applicable watch points.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Executed rollout, publish, export, or handoff with explicit boundary outcome, rollback/removal status, and watch notes where applicable.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Operator notes, artifact placement or deployment receipt, applicable telemetry or smoke checkpoints, not-applicable entries for out-of-boundary production controls, and any rollback, removal, or release halt.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release manager may execute only inside the approved boundary, window, and rollback-trigger limits.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Trigger halt, rollback, removal, or no-go immediately when applicable telemetry, artifact integrity, user impact, data impact, or operational constraints breach the approved threshold. Do not block for missing public deployment, CI, or production telemetry when the approved boundary is a package or output-folder handoff.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Execution ownership remains with the release-manager role until rollout completes or fails.
Implementation owner stays available for rapid corrective interpretation during rollout.
Governance owner reviews telemetry and escalation timing during the release window.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Deployment, handoff, and watch log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident replay and release retrospectives.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture release timing, artifact placement or deployment receipt, applicable telemetry or smoke checkpoints, not-applicable out-of-boundary controls, and any halt, rollback, or removal decision.

Steps.Title: Capture first-pass post-release learning

Steps.OutputContractSummary: Post-release learning review with corrective actions and simulation updates.

Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns follow-up assignment while architecture and release roles retain responsibility for their own control gaps.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close the process while critical corrective actions remain unnamed or unowned.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Follow-up ownership remains explicit until corrective actions have accountable owners.
Architecture role reviews systemic design findings rather than only local defects.
Release role reviews telemetry and rollback-control lessons.

Steps.Title: Perform security review after repair
Steps.Subtitle: Sensitive data, secrets, and exception posture
Steps.Notes: Review trust-boundary, dependency, secrets, and data-handling impact after the repaired QA path is accepted. Scale findings to the declared release boundary instead of inventing production controls that are outside the approved handoff.
Steps.InputContractSummary: QA-accepted repaired package, changed-surface inventory, repair notes, and data-handling notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Security outcome with explicit approval, block, or exception rationale tied to the declared release boundary.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security review notes, exception rationale, boundary-applicable controls, and future production controls when they are outside the current boundary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer owns the sign-off for sensitive-data and boundary-applicable policy exceptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block release when repaired current-boundary data-handling review capacity is missing, exception rationale is incomplete, or a security risk affects the approved handoff. Record out-of-boundary production controls as recommendations unless explicitly required.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security approval remains attached to the role even if the reviewer changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Security exception assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release governance, audit, and post-incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture boundary-applicable controls, residual risk owner, approval or block rationale, and any future controls that are not release blockers for the current boundary.

Steps.Title: Record repaired .NET run commands under process run node
Steps.Subtitle: Run command, Run app, Run tests
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe runtime command writeback after repaired QA acceptance. Refresh or confirm runtime-capable Run app and Run tests nodes under the current process run node using repaired evidence. Runnable commands must use Environment, Script, or Infrastructure node types with runtime metadata, not delivery blocks. The child handoff must include launcher-compatible metadata receipts for every runnable command node; do not accept a Run app or Run tests node as repaired when it lacks the project path, command, arguments, working directory, subtype, or other metadata needed by the project-structure runtime launcher.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Accepted QA evidence, architecture handoff, implementation evidence, and process run node context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed .NET runtime command project-structure writeback child run with parent-ready evidence for runtime-capable Run app and Run tests nodes.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, managed artifacts, project-structure receipts, node ids, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Parent role coordinates subprocess completion and cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Inspect stopped child subprocess evidence before blocking. If required child evidence is missing and relaunch is allowed, relaunch through the subprocess driver; block only for concrete missing tools, inputs, policy/environment failures, or irrecoverable evidence after a fresh child result.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a role-compatible operator that can observe the subprocess and record parent evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET Run command writeback after repair
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by release approval and process-run replay.

Steps.Title: Capture and store repaired .NET UI screenshots
Steps.Subtitle: Screenshots under process run node
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe UI screenshot writeback after repaired runtime command nodes exist. UI targets must store repaired screenshots under Screenshots below the process run node; no-UI targets must carry explicit no-UI evidence. When a child screenshot handoff accepts or rejects repaired screenshots for visual reasons, verify that the child evidence includes current-run `workspace_analyze_image` receipts for individual screenshots and `workspace_analyze_images` receipts for ordered comparisons or time-dependent behavior. Do not complete from screenshot paths, dimensions, or project-structure image asset ids alone when the downstream decision depends on visual content. Write the parent step record to artifacts/process-runs/<current-process-run-id>/steps/capture-ui-screenshots-after-repair.md and include that exact path in final evidenceRefs together with child screenshot handoff evidence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Accepted QA evidence, architecture handoff, implementation evidence, and process run node context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed .NET UI screenshot project-structure writeback child run with parent-ready writeback evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, managed artifacts, provider-backed image-analysis receipts for repaired visual screenshot decisions, project-structure receipts, node ids, screenshot or no-UI receipts, runtime command compatibility evidence, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Parent role coordinates subprocess completion and cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Inspect stopped child subprocess evidence before blocking. LocalRoles.Summary: Migration-specific authority for schema, data backfill, and rollback safety.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Own all migration mechanics that can compromise data integrity, rollback realism, or release sequencing.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A specialist engineer who understands the data model, operational windows, and migration rollback implications in depth.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Migration-specific authority for schema, data backfill, and rollback safety.
KnowledgeRequirements: Deep knowledge of schema evolution, data backfill sequencing, locking behavior, and rollback limitations.
Understanding of production data sensitivity, replication, and consistency risk during change rollout.
Ability to design reversible migration patterns or explicitly document when reversal is not technically safe.
Knowledge of runbook requirements for staged or data-bearing change.
Ability to interpret telemetry that indicates migration success, degradation, or partial failure.
Understanding of how code and migration deployment order interact.
ExperienceRequirements: Has executed or reviewed production data migrations with rollback planning.
Has investigated migration-related incidents or degraded performance after release.
Has coordinated schema changes across application and platform teams.
Has authored or reviewed migration runbooks consumed by operators.
Has signed off data integrity evidence before production deployment.
DecisionRights: Approve migration sequence and rollback viability.
Block release when migration evidence is incomplete or unsafe.
Define environment, user-segment, or batch sequencing constraints for deployment.
Escalate when data change risk exceeds the normal release window.
CollaborationExpectations: Work closely with platform engineer, release approver, and software engineer.
Provide QA with data-risk hotspots requiring targeted validation.
Coordinate with service owner on maintenance-window and support implications.
Document exactly what 'successful migration' means operationally.
AntiPatterns: Treating rollback as a theoretical possibility instead of a rehearsed path.
Approving data change based only on lower-environment success.
Ignoring long-running lock or backfill side effects.
Bundling unrelated schema risk into one opaque change.
FitnessEvidence: Reviewed migration plans with explicit rollback reasoning.
Evidence of successful migration rehearsals or controlled dry runs.
Incident learnings showing the role reduced data-change risk.
Clear operator-facing runbooks owned by the role.

LocalRoles.Summary: Owner for end-user enablement, release notes clarity, and operational adoption readiness.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Ensure release output is accompanied by the minimal training, release notes, and internal enablement needed for successful adoption.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A delivery or enablement specialist who can turn technical change into usable guidance for affected users and support teams.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Owner for end-user enablement, release notes clarity, and operational adoption readiness.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior enablement or operations readiness specialist
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to identify what users, support, and customer-facing teams need to understand before or immediately after release.
Knowledge of release notes design, training format selection, and stakeholder communication timing.
Understanding of adoption friction caused by missing documentation or ambiguous behavior changes.
Ability to extract accurate behavior deltas from engineering and product input.
Knowledge of support-readiness and knowledge-base update workflows.
Ability to define minimum enablement completeness criteria.
ExperienceRequirements: Has owned training or enablement deliverables for a software launch or major feature.
Has coordinated release-note or support-content updates with technical teams.
Has handled rollout where adoption risk was driven by user misunderstanding rather than technical defect.
Has updated internal support teams on changed workflows or known caveats.
Has measured or at least qualitatively assessed readiness gaps after release.
DecisionRights: Approve completion of required enablement artifacts before broad rollout.
Require documentation updates for behavior changes that affect users or support.
Escalate if release timing would make support or adoption chaos likely.
Declare whether a limited rollout can proceed without full broad-audience training.
CollaborationExpectations: Collaborate with product owner, customer success, and QA on customer-facing clarity.
Work with engineers to make technical change understandable without distortion.
Coordinate with service owner for support window planning.
Feed adoption pain back into retrospective improvements.
AntiPatterns: Treating release notes as marketing copy instead of operational guidance.
Publishing training content that does not match the implemented behavior.
Declaring readiness because documentation exists, regardless of usefulness.
Ignoring support-team readiness for changed workflows.
FitnessEvidence: Adoption artifacts consumed successfully by customer-facing teams.
Release note and training materials with explicit behavioral changes.
Evidence of reduced support confusion after guided releases.
Retrospective feedback showing the role improved adoption readiness.

LocalRoles.Summary: Implementation owner for code, tests, migration notes, and reviewable delivery proof.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Own the change set and keep implementation evidence aligned with the approved architecture and release boundary.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: Build-capable engineering owner for the working change set and adjacent test evidence.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Implementation owner for code, tests, migration notes, and executable delivery proof.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior software engineer or technical lead
KnowledgeRequirements: Solid command of the target codebase language, architecture conventions, and test approach.
Understanding of version control, code review, CI pipelines, and release hygiene.
Ability to interpret architecture guidance and convert it into implementable tasks without scope drift.
Knowledge of defect prevention techniques, observability basics, and safe rollback-friendly change packaging.
Ability to produce evidence that links what changed to why it is safe enough to proceed.
Understanding of secure coding and dependency hygiene expectations for the stack in use.
ExperienceRequirements: Has delivered production code with automated test coverage and peer review evidence.
Has decomposed medium-complexity work into implementable slices with clear review boundaries.
Has debugged at least one production issue or high-severity defect linked to code they worked on.
Has participated in release or deployment readiness discussions and adjusted code accordingly.
Has collaborated with QA and architecture reviewers to repair inadequate evidence or design drift.
DecisionRights: Choose implementation approach within approved architectural guardrails.
Stop and escalate when required inputs, access, or environment assumptions are missing.
Recommend technical debt acceptance or rejection when delivery pressure appears.
Refuse AI-generated output that cannot be validated to the required standard.
CollaborationExpectations: Clarify ambiguity with product and architecture roles before making silent assumptions.
Provide QA and reviewers with concrete evidence, not only assertions of completion.
Document trade-offs when delivery timing forces constrained implementation choices.
Support incident and hotfix response for changes the engineer helped deliver.
AntiPatterns: Treating passing local tests as sufficient release evidence.
Shipping code that depends on tacit environment knowledge no one else has.
Accepting AI-generated code without line-level comprehension and verification.
FitnessEvidence: Merged changes with traceable test and review evidence.
Examples of defect analysis or incident participation showing engineering accountability.
Consistent adherence to repository conventions and delivery guardrails.
Code reviews from peers indicating clarity, maintainability, and risk awareness.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Evidence pack from rehearsal or dry-run execution of a risky schema or data migration.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release approval, rollback review, and post-release forensic analysis only for the covered migration path.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must show rehearsal scope, dataset assumptions, timing, and rollback observations.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Confirms the delivery scope is stable enough for downstream QA, training, and release work.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: Implementation is materially complete and release-sensitive downstream work is starting.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Scope change after this point is either rejected or explicitly re-opened with re-planning.
Checks: Release-candidate scope is named and versioned.
Late additions are either rejected or explicitly accepted with impact review.
QA, training, and release owners were informed of the frozen scope baseline.
Open defects and known exclusions are captured.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms risky data or schema migration behavior was rehearsed credibly before production exposure.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Rehearsal covered realistic sequencing, timing, and rollback observations for the declared risk slice.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Migration assumptions remain theoretical or rehearsal omitted critical risk characteristics.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to release approver and service owner; block production rollout until addressed.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for turning raw change and defect notes into a final scope recap for downstream reviewers.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to present scope as frozen if unresolved changes are still entering the branch.
